subsystems.name: Solar array
subsystems.role: collects sunlight continuously in orbit, where there is no night, cloud or atmosphere.
parts: lightweight photovoltaic blankets or concentrator panels

subsystems.name: Power conversion and transmitter
subsystems.role: converts DC electricity into a microwave beam and shapes it into a steerable aperture.

subsystems.name: Structure and attitude control
subsystems.role: holds a structure kilometres across pointing precisely at one spot on Earth.

subsystems.name: Beam control and safety
subsystems.role: aims the beam at the receiver and proves it cannot wander onto people or aircraft.

subsystems.name: Rectenna and grid interface
subsystems.role: converts the arriving microwave power back to DC electricity and feeds the grid.

subsystems.name: Assembly and orbit infrastructure
subsystems.role: gets thousands of tonnes of hardware from the ground into the right orbit and puts it together.

buildSteps.title: Close the link budget
buildSteps.detail: Calculate what fraction of sunlight ends up as grid electricity: array efficiency, DC-to-RF conversion, beam spreading over 35,786 km to geostationary orbit, atmospheric loss, and rectenna conversion. Typical designs land well under 20% end to end, which sets how vast the satellite must be.

buildSteps.title: Make modular tiles
buildSteps.detail: Rather than one giant machine, manufacture identical solar-and-transmitter panels on production lines, each able to be handled by a robot and plugged into a power and data bus.

buildSteps.title: Launch the pieces
buildSteps.detail: Heavy-lift reusable rockets would carry hundreds or thousands of tonnes of panels, trusses and cables to low orbit; the cost per kilogram, not the physics, is the main gate.

buildSteps.title: Assemble in orbit
buildSteps.detail: Robot arms or free-flying robots connect modules into a phased array and raise the finished satellite from low orbit to geostationary altitude, or assemble it there directly.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate the beam
buildSteps.detail: A pilot signal sent up from the rectenna lets the array measure and correct the phase of every element, so the beam focuses on the receiver instead of spreading.

buildSteps.title: Build the rectenna
buildSteps.detail: On the ground, lay out the dipole-and-diode array over many square kilometres — thin, mostly transparent to sunlight, so the land can often be shared with farming.

buildSteps.title: Beam at low power first
buildSteps.detail: Start at a small fraction of design power with aircraft and spectrum authorities monitoring, verifying that a failed array or drifting satellite leaves the beam defocused and harmless.

buildSteps.title: Ramp up and connect
buildSteps.detail: Raise power in steps as efficiency and safety are proven, then hand a steady, dispatchable supply to the grid like any baseload plant.

prerequisites.why: a power satellite weighs tens of thousands of tonnes; today's launch prices make the electricity hopelessly expensive.
space stations and servicing missions have joined modules robotically, but nothing kilometre-scale has been built autonomously.
microwave beaming has been demonstrated between ground stations and, in 2023, from a small satellite to Earth, but not at megawatt scale through the atmosphere.
arrays with far higher power per kilogram than today's are needed to keep launch mass down.
power beaming at gigawatt levels crosses aviation, communications and radio-astronomy interests that no framework yet covers.

prerequisites.tech: Grid-scale rectenna sites and grid access
prerequisites.why: the receiving land is ordinary real estate and the grid connection is conventional — the constraint is public acceptance, not technology.

pathway.milestone: component demonstrations: in-space wireless power transfer from a small satellite (2023) and ground-based microwave transmission tests
pathway.unlocks: proof that the transmitter, beam steering and rectenna work outside the laboratory.

pathway.milestone: a dedicated demonstration satellite beaming kilowatts to a ground rectenna, with independent safety verification
pathway.unlocks: real end-to-end efficiency numbers and a regulatory precedent.

pathway.milestone: robotically assembled megawatt-class platforms in low or geostationary orbit
pathway.unlocks: in-space assembly, servicing and station-keeping experience at scale.

pathway.milestone: a pilot geostationary plant delivering hundreds of megawatts to one grid
pathway.unlocks: a price and performance baseline for deciding whether fleets are worth building.

pathway.milestone: multiple plants supplying firm power to markets with poor renewables
pathway.unlocks: continuous, weather-independent clean electricity — if launch cost keeps falling.
